subject: Re: Terminology sign-off: Structured output (public docs) + model support language
body:
From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Terminology sign-off: Structured output (public docs) + model support language

Hey Nikhil,

We’re ready to publish the structured output guide updates as part of the streaming/tools examples refresh, but want a final PM pass on:

1) Public terminology (we’ve seen “JSON mode” / “schema-constrained” / “structured output” floating around)
2) The model support language (what we claim, what we caveat)

Draft is in PR 527: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-docs/pull/527

The current top-of-page copy:
- Heading: “Structured output (JSON schema)”
- Definition: “Return responses that validate against a JSON schema.”
- Caveat: “Behavior varies by model. We recommend validating client-side and retrying on schema violations.”

Two specific questions:
- Should we avoid the phrase “guarantee” entirely and stick to “best-effort + validate”? 
- For the support matrix (PM-413), we currently say “Supported on Redwood Verified models” and “Limited/experimental on others.” Does that match what you want to promise?

If you can reply with wording edits (or just ‘approved’), we’ll merge + ship.

Thanks,
Elliot

—
Elliot Price
Director, Technical Documentation
Redwood Inference



From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 9:36 AM PST
Subject: Re: Terminology sign-off: Structured output (public docs) + model support language

Thanks — read through PR 527.

Requested edits (mainly to avoid over-promising + reduce support tickets):

Terminology
- Let’s standardize on “Structured output” as the primary term.
- Use “JSON schema” in the subtitle / parameter docs (technical precision), but avoid “JSON mode” as a heading. “JSON mode” has OpenAI-compat baggage and people infer stronger guarantees than we intend.
- “Schema-constrained” is fine in a single sentence as a synonym, but not as the core branding.

Support language
- Yes, please avoid “guarantee” globally.
- Suggest we use:
  - “Schema-constrained structured output” on Redwood Verified models (link to the model catalog entry)
  - “Best-effort structured output” on other compatible models

I’d also like one explicit line that says something like:
- “Always validate the response with your own schema validator. If validation fails, retry with the same schema and a short ‘fix the JSON’ instruction.”

Minor: In the “Streaming + structured output” section, add a warning that partial chunks are not valid JSON and users should only parse after final.

Monica: any concerns from the SDK side with the proposed language? (just checking for mismatch with examples)

-Nikhil

—
Nikhil Sharma
Director of Product, Hosted API
Redwood Inference



From: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 10:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Terminology sign-off: Structured output (public docs) + model support language

+1 to Nikhil’s edits.

On the model support matrix wording (PM-413), I recommend we be very explicit about what “supported” means:
- “Supported” = SDKs/docs have tested examples + we monitor regressions via evals
- Not “supported” = might work but not something Support will treat as a bug if the model outputs invalid JSON

Also adding one nuance that’s bitten users:
- When tool calling is enabled, models can sometimes emit tool calls *instead of* the JSON you asked for. We should advise customers to either (a) disable tools for the structured-output step, or (b) route the final formatting step to a model/profile that’s stable for JSON schema.

If that’s too much for the intro, it could go in “Known pitfalls.”

Wei

—
Wei Chen
Hosted API Documentation
Redwood Inference



From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 10:24 AM PST
Subject: Re: Terminology sign-off: Structured output (public docs) + model support language

Agree with the direction.

Two things from a DevEx perspective:
1) Keep the top-of-page copy simple: “Structured output” + “validate + retry.” Don’t lead with compatibility disclaimers, but do make them unmissable.
2) Please ensure the examples in docs match the released SDK semantics (streaming final assembly, parse only on final). We’re trying to eliminate ‘copy/paste’ failures.

If we can land Nikhil’s terminology edits + Wei’s “supported means tested/monitored” clarification, I’m comfortable signing off from DX.

-Alex

—
Alex Martinez
VP, Developer Experience
Redwood Inference



From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 11:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Terminology sign-off: Structured output (public docs) + model support language

Approved with the edits below.

Final wording guidance (please implement in PR 527):

A) Terminology
- Title: “Structured output”
- Subtitle: “JSON schema”
- First mention: “Structured output (schema-constrained JSON)”
- Avoid: “JSON mode” (ok to mention once in an OpenAI-compat footnote if needed, but not as a primary term)

B) Model support language
- Use “Redwood Verified models: schema-constrained structured output (tested + monitored)”
- Use “Other compatible models: best-effort structured output (validate + retry recommended)”
- Don’t use “guaranteed” anywhere.

C) Required callouts
- Add explicit warning: “Streaming chunks are not valid JSON. Only parse after the final response is assembled.”
- Add explicit recommendation: “Always validate the response. On validation failure, retry with the same schema and a brief correction instruction.”

Wei’s tool-calling interaction note can go in Known pitfalls (good idea).

Once those are in, consider this PM sign-off to publish.

-Nikhil
